page.title: Best Budget Anamorphic Lens (2026): SIRUI 50mm F1.8 1.33x vs Venus, Astra and Blazar Beetle
page.desc: The cheapest real anamorphic lens worth buying, which one works on full frame, which has autofocus, and what owners complain about. Prices checked 2026-11-06.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best budget anamorphic lens is the SIRUI 50mm F1.8 1.33x ({buy:sirui-50mm-f1-8-1-33x-anamorphic}): a real anamorphic prime with an f/1.8 aperture and a 1.33x squeeze that turns a 16:9 frame into 2.4:1 widescreen with no crop, at a third of the price of the next-cheapest new anamorphic lens. The catch: it covers Super 35 / APS-C and Micro Four Thirds only, so on a full-frame body you shoot in the camera's APS-C crop mode or you get dark corners. It is also manual focus with no electronic contacts, and it focuses no closer than 2.8 ft.

If you shoot full frame and want the cheapest way in, the SIRUI Venus 50mm T2.9 1.6x ({buy:sirui-venus-50mm-t2-9-1-6x-anamorphic}) covers a full-frame sensor with a stronger 1.6x squeeze, at the cost of 2.27 lb of weight. If you need autofocus, the SIRUI Astra 50mm T1.8 1.33x ({buy:sirui-astra-50mm-t1-8-1-33x-af-anamorphic}) is the cheapest full-frame anamorphic lens with AF we found. If you want small and light on full frame, the Blazar Beetle 45mm T3.2 1.33x is 0.59 lb but two stops slower. For a phone, the Moment Anamorphic 1.33x Mobile Lens II costs $150 at Moment (seen 2026-11-06) and needs a Moment T-Series case.
page.after:
What owners complain about

We read the CineD, RedShark and sonyalpha.blog reviews, the EOSHD owner thread and retailer reviews for the SIRUI 1.33x line and its rivals. Counts are mentions across those sources.

  • Dark corners on full frame (6). The 1.33x line is a Super 35 design. Sony a7 owners use APS-C crop or 1.3x to 1.5x Clear Image Zoom. One a7S III owner still saw slight vignetting on one side and returned the lens.
  • The look is subtle (4). 1.33x gives mild oval bokeh and modest streaks. Reviewers call it natural rather than fake. One buyer called the effect negligible at close range. The 1.6x Venus and Saturn lenses exist for that reason.
  • Manual focus, no lens data (3). No electronic contacts, so you rely on peaking. The focus throw is 143.6 degrees.
  • 2.8 ft close focus (3). Reviewers wished it focused closer. Close-up filters to +10 work; extension tubes do not.
  • Squeeze drifts with focus on the wider lenses (2). Owners of the 24mm and 35mm report the ratio moving between about 1.25x and 1.33x through the focus range. The 50mm reviews do not report this.
  • Flares (2). Streaks are blue only, and strong top light causes veiling glare without a matte box.
  • Markings and gears (1). Focus and iris marks are faint, and there are no 0.8 mod gears in the box.

Which one by need

  • Crop-sensor camera, first anamorphic: the SIRUI 50mm F1.8 1.33x. On a Sony FX30, a Fujifilm X body or a Panasonic Micro Four Thirds body it needs no crop. The FX30 (firmware 2.00 and up) and the Panasonic S5 II and G9 II show a 1.33x de-squeezed preview in camera.
  • Full-frame body, lowest price: the SIRUI Venus 50mm T2.9 1.6x. Shoot 3:2 open gate for 2.4:1 or 16:9 for 2.8:1. The Sony FX3 (firmware 7.00) and FX30 (6.00) can preview 1.6x. Panasonic bodies offer 1.5x and 1.8x but not 1.6x, so you preview squeezed or use a monitor.
  • Full frame, small and light: the Blazar Beetle 45mm T3.2 1.33x at $599 (Blazar store, 2026-11-06) weighs 0.59 lb and focuses to 1.5 ft, but T3.2 is two stops slower than the SIRUI. SIRUI's own Saturn V2 50mm at $599 (SIRUI store, 2026-11-06) is T2.9, 1.6x, about 1.07 lb, and rotates 90 degrees for vertical video.
  • Autofocus: the SIRUI Astra 50mm T1.8 1.33x. Blazar's Talon 35mm T2.1 1.5x AF is $1,099 (Blazar store, 2026-11-06).
  • Phone: the Moment Anamorphic 1.33x Mobile Lens II, $150 at Moment (2026-11-06), with a T-Series case.

Not recommended for a first anamorphic

  • Anamorphic adapters such as the SIRUI 1.25x ($299, SIRUI store, 2026-11-06), the Blazar Nero 1.5x ($999, out of stock on 2026-11-06) or a vintage Iscorama: two-lens stacks that need alignment and double focusing. Good for tinkerers, slow for finishing a project.
  • Laowa Nanomorph 1.5x from $999 per lens (laowacine.com, 2026-11-06): tiny and well regarded, but five times the SIRUI's price and still Super 35.
  • 2x sets such as the Blazar Cato four-lens set ($2,599, Blazar store, 2026-11-06): they need a 4:3 open-gate camera and are overkill at this budget.
